\begin{table}[t]

  \caption{\textbf{Propagation throughput --- the engine, isolated from the sampler.} Boolean implications per second: GPAP's from the packed-word kernel, CMSGen's from its own counters (\texttt{--statsevery}, \texttt{scripts/cmsgen\_gpap\_eval.patch}). The identity $\text{samples/s ratio} = \text{impl/s ratio} \,/\, \text{work-per-sample ratio}$ holds on every family. It is an ALGEBRAIC identity, not a validation --- defining work-per-sample as the quotient of the two rates makes it true by construction, so it can only fail if an aggregation mixes row sets, which is exactly the per-column-filtering error it is here to catch. What it does is factor the sample-rate result into what the GPU propagator buys and what rejection sampling spends: GPAP discards a conflicted trajectory outright, whereas CMSGen backtracks and retains the partial work. GPAP's implication rate is nearly constant across families; the three-orders-of-magnitude spread in Table~\ref{tab:cmsgen} therefore comes from the work-per-sample column, not from the propagator. $n$ counts instances where \emph{both} samplers emitted, since a work-per-sample figure needs both; $^{\ddagger}$marks rows where that leaves fewer than three.}
